newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond options vols mainly flat.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond options vols mainly flat.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond futures-options were basically flat Wednesday heading into Thursday's June U.S. jobs report.

Although many pundits had looked for quiet range-trade, some said futures had moved further in both directions the last few days than they would have expected before the data, and they also noted buying of gamma before the jobs figures.

"The last couple of days, we have had one-plus standard deviation moves," said one T-bond options floor broker. "So the guys who are long options and long gamma...are getting paid...the effect of gamma is outweighing the time decay."
Another broker quoted August at-the-money bond volatility at 7.8/7.9 percent, basically unchanged, with September off a hair at 7.8/8.0 percent.
Featured trades Wednesday included one commission house that sold 10,000 August 114 bond calls, about 13 delta, at about 7.25 percent vol, brokers said.

Another firm bought 10,000 August 111/112 put spreads at 28/64 as it rolled long 111 puts up to the 112 strike to give itself the most gamma exposure heading into Thursday's jobs report, the second broker said.
The firm bought 7.90 percent vol and sold 8.05 percent vol at 21 delta. "It's position-maintenance and rolling up strikes...to stay at-the-money before the jobs data," she added.
In the over-the-counter market, a large hedge fund bought $3 billion one-week at-the-money two-year note puts at about a price of 99.30-plus, she said.
She said that put pressure on the old two-year note and also weighed on two-year T-note futures earlier in the day.

In Eurodollars, a broker said a dealer drew attention when it bought 3,000 December 94.25/94.50 call spreads and sold 3,000 December 93.50 puts against it as a cabinet credit. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
